title: Token floor + sprint hiring experiment
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This is a short-run experiment proposal and scratch model to test a token-price floor combined with a 12-week sprint hiring plan (temp contractors + selective FTEs) to protect gross margin in a down-market while maintaining capacity for enterprise bursts. Goal: quantify breakeven token volumes, required HC mix, and sensitivity to price moves so leadership can sign off on a contingency runway.

Status: draft, numbers are preliminary. Model owner: Sofia R. (finance). Primary ask: review assumptions and flag obvious misses.

Key constraints and context:
- Hosted API demand has become more variable; enterprise customers want burst guarantees.
- We must avoid knee-jerk hiring that increases fixed cost when token price compression persists.
- Operational requirement: keep 99th percentile latency SLO for premium routes.

Assumptions (baseline month):
- Baseline revenue: $2.45M / month (all products aggregated)
- Baseline cost-of-goods (COGS, infra + GPU ops): $1.15M / month
- Current effective token price (avg rev per 1k tokens): $0.045
- Current tokens served: ~54B tokens / month equivalent
- Personnel included in COGS (ops, serving eng time allocation): 32 FTEs prorated; personnel cost in COGS $420k/mo
- Available contingency hiring budget (headroom without board approval): $420k / month (contract and temporary mix)

Baseline P&L (monthly, rounded):
- Revenue: $2,450,000
- COGS: $1,150,000 (infra $730k, personnel $420k)
- Gross margin: $1,300,000 (53%)
- OpEx (non-COGS): $820,000
- Net: $480,000

Experiment framework (12-week sprint):
Objective: maintain capability to serve enterprise bursts (peak capacity up to +40% tokens on premium routes) while protecting margin if token prices compress by 10-40%.
Options modeled:
- Option A (Lean): 0 net FTEs, use contractors for burst ops (estimated cost $140k/mo when active), preserve $250k buffer in infra.
- Option B (Hybrid): +6 FTEs (2 serving eng, 2 SRE, 2 infra ops) phased over 12 weeks + limited contractors; incremental personnel cost $180k/mo fully ramped.
- Option C (Aggressive): +12 FTEs permanent, to permanently increase throughput and reduce third-party contractor reliance; incremental personnel cost $360k/mo.

Base-case throughput safety: need to be able to cover +40% peak tokens for premium customers for up to 72 hours without violating SLOs. That drives temporary GPU reservation cost of ~$95k per major burst event (one-time per event).

Pricing sensitivity scenarios (impact on monthly P&L):
Scenario inputs: token price change: -10%, -25%, -40%. We hold token volume constant for sensitivity to isolate price pressure (volume elasticity handled in separate model).
Quick sensitivity outputs (rounded):
- -10% token price:
  - Revenue: $2,205,000 (-$245k)
  - Gross margin: $1,055,000 (47.8%)
  - Net: $435,000 (net down 9%)
  - Required contingency draw to maintain OpEx cushion: ~none if Lean option used, but contractor usage eats ~$60k/mo from buffer.
- -25% token price:
  - Revenue: $1,837,500 (-$612.5k)
  - Gross margin: $692,500 (37.7%)
  - Net: $-127,500 (monthly loss)
  - Recommended action: trigger hybrid hiring freeze; implement token-floor promotion for top-of-funnel; consider temporary infra cost cuts.
- -40% token price:
  - Revenue: $1,470,000 (-$980k)
  - Gross margin: $235,000 (16%)
  - Net: $-585,000
  - Recommended action: immediate draw on contingency hiring budget, pause noncritical infra projects, negotiate reserved capacity pricing with cloud vendors, implement stepped price floor for new customers.

Headcount tradeoffs (qualitative + numbers):
- Contractors vs FTEs: contractors give flexibility for 12-week bursts but are ~1.6x per-hour more expensive and have lower institutional knowledge. FTEs reduce marginal long-run unit cost but increase fixed burden and reduce runway.
- Skills prioritized if hiring: serving runtime performance engineers (2), SRE with autoscaling expertise (2), infra cost-optimization engineer (1), short-term capacity manager/PM (1). Total: 6 (Hybrid case).

Breakeven token price calculation (simple):
- Fixed non-COGS and fixed personnel in COGS = $1,150,000 - (variable infra per-token estimate)
- Approx variable infra per 1k tokens currently = $0.0046 (backsolve: infra $730k / 54B * 1k)
- Breakeven price per 1k tokens to preserve current gross margin (assuming volumes constant) ~ $0.028. (i.e., if price falls below 2.8 cents/1k tokens, we need to cut capacity or reduce personnel)

Quick-run risk map (notes):
- Risk: token price declines >25% + volume drop => negative net within one month. Likelihood: medium-high given market signals.
- Mitigant: temporary token-floor promotions for high-usage customers (short-term revenue protection, may slow new signups) and pre-negotiate paused-hire clauses with recruiting.

Operational checklist for a triggered -25% price event (playbook):
- T+0 (first 72 hours): convene crisis pod (FP&A, Head of Hosting, Head of SRE, CTO). Implement 10% immediate non-essential infra throttle to reclaim $60-120k.
- T+1 week: freeze noncritical hires. Defer two planned infra projects. Activate contractor pool to cover critical burst windows only.
- T+3 weeks: decide on hybrid hiring vs layoffs depending on recovery signals. Initiate customer-level price-floor program (opt-in).

Open questions / TODOs (please weigh in):
- How elastic is enterprise burst demand? If volume falls with price, revenue hit could be worse; need customer-level elastics (Amit to provide by 3/19).
- Are there immediate contractual obligations for Dedicated customers that force capacity retention? (Legal/CS to confirm).
- Can we reduce per-burst GPU reservation cost via multi-tenant scheduling or pre-negotiated spot pools? (Infra to validate).

Recommended next steps (week-by-week):
- Week 0: sanity-check assumptions above with Infra (Arjun) and Hosting PM (Lila).
- Week 1: build a simple sensitivity spreadsheet that ties token price, volume elasticity, and HC mix into weekly burn and runway (owner: Sofia).
- Week 2: leadership review of the 12-week sprint experiment and sign-off on the contingency spend floor.
- Week 3-12: if signed, execute Hybrid option as phased contractor->FTE conversion with weekly financial gates.

Notes to reviewers: numbers intentionally conservative for margin calculation. This doc is intended as an experiment skeleton rather than a final exec brief. Please leave inline comments in the model sheet (linked artifacts) or ping me in #fin-planning.
